column1: # hypothesis: Conley index theory is a robust
column2: computer-assisted alternative to Morse theory that tolerates degenerate critical points
column4: Haas & Lipinski on Conley-Morse persistence barcodes at 0.662. It requires an isolating neighbourhood around the invariant set
column5: and box_exact has exactly-equal samples across whole faces
column6: so gradf = 0 on a set of positive measure and no isolating neighbourhood exists -- the method is undefined precisely where it would be needed. (C1) The plateau fraction is measured per field
column7: quantifying the obstruction rather than asserting it. (C2) The fraction of cells where an isolating neighbourhood exists is reported
column8: and compared against the fraction where discrete Morse theory -- already registered -- applies
column9: so the two are ranked on the same data rather than on argument. SHARE: none -- this closes a candidate.

column1: # falsified by: C1 by negligible plateaus on every field
column2: which would revive the method and make this row a false alarm worth having raised. C2 by Conley applying more widely than discrete Morse
column3: which would reverse the ranking. VACUITY CONTROL: box_exact must report a non-zero plateau fraction
column4: or the obstruction this row is built on does not exist in the fixture.
